paragraphs: A line drawn somewhere in eternity.

What if I’m not in it?
What if I missed it?
What if heaven already counted… and I didn’t make the list?
Because this number in Revelation doesn’t just reveal something about heaven…
We don’t say it out loud.

When we fail again.
When we fall into the same secret sin.
When we pray… but feel nothing.
“Maybe salvation is for the better ones.”
“Maybe God has a quota… and I’m not qualified.”
We polish the outside while the inside whispers:
“Then I heard the number of those who were sealed: 144,000…”
But just a few verses later—
“After this I looked, and there before me was a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people and language…”
Some scholars interpret the 144,000 as a literal group.
Because God is speaking to our fear.
THE REAL PROBLEM ISN’T THE NUMBER
Because we know how broken we are.
That version of us no one sees.
“God must be limiting access… because I don’t deserve unlimited grace.”
THE GOSPEL TURN — THIS CHANGES EVERYTHING
“They have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.”
You are not counted in because you are clean.
Because Jesus was crushed for you.
“He was pierced for our transgressions… and by His wounds we are healed.”
“For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith… not by works, so that no one can boast.”
But by the Lamb who was slain.
Because the real dividing line is not a number.
“I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
The one who thinks you’ve gone too far.
The one who keeps failing in secret.
The cross of Jesus is not a closed list.
“Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
Stop trying to earn what Jesus already paid for.
Let His blood wash what your effort never could.
Let His grace rewrite what shame tried to finalize.
